papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data from long-read sequencing, which better captures full-length transcripts and alternative splicing than short reads. Using paired short-read and Nanopore long-read datasets, the authors systematically evaluate tool performance, providing guidance for method selection.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of an antibody dependent cellular phagocytosis related signature for hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The reduced phagocytic activity of macrophages in the tumor microenvironment (TME) and the presence of anti-phagocytic factors in cancer cells hinder the effectiveness of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in clinical settings. Consequently, our objective was to create a risk assessment model using antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) regulators to serve as prognostic indicators and immunotherapy markers for individuals with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
papers.summary: This study developed a risk assessment model based on antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) regulators to predict prognosis and immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Using multi-omics data, the authors identified a signature that could serve as a prognostic indicator and help guide immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

papers.title: Single-cell mitophagy patterns dictate intercellular crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment to promote osteosarcoma progression.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is a highly aggressive primary bone malignancy in adolescents, with poor prognosis due to limited diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of cancer, and mitophagy, the selective clearance of damaged mitochondria, critically maintains cellular homeostasis. However, the specific role of mitophagy in shaping the OS tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution remains poorly understood. This study aims to systematically characterize mitophagy patterns within the OS TME and investigate their impact on intercellular communication, tu
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes mitophagy patterns at single-cell resolution in osteosarcoma, revealing how mitochondrial clearance shapes intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment to drive cancer progression. The findings highlight mitophagy as a key regulator of tumor-stroma crosstalk, offering potential new diagnostic and therapeutic targets for this aggressive bone cancer.

papers.title: A Simple, Cost-Effective, High-Throughput Method for Measuring Chromatin Accessibility and Gene Expression in Single Nuclei.
papers.abstract: We describe microfluidic-free, droplet-based methods for single-nucleus epigenomic measurements: Particle-templated Instant Partition single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (PIP-ATAC-seq) and its multiomic version (PIP-Multiome-seq). We benchmarked these assays by generating data sets containing thousands of nuclei using cell lines and mouse brains and compared to other established methods. PIP-Multiome and PIP-ATAC are straightforward to implement, affordable, and produce high-quality data, providing useful additions to the single-cell molecular measurement
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces PIP-ATAC-seq and PIP-Multiome-seq, new microfluidic-free, droplet-based methods for measuring chromatin accessibility and gene expression in single nuclei. These methods are cost-effective, easy to implement, and produce high-quality data comparable to established techniques, making them valuable tools for single-cell epigenomic research.

papers.title: CAdir: Joint clustering of cells and genes for single-cell transcriptomics with visualization-driven cluster quality assessment.
papers.abstract: Clustering for single-cell RNA-seq aims at finding similar cells and grouping them into biologically meaningful clusters. Many available clustering algorithms however do not not provide the cluster defining marker genes or are unable to infer the number of clusters in an unsupervised manner as well as lack tools to easily determine the quality of the label assignments. Therefore, clustering quality is commonly evaluated by visually inspecting low-dimensional embeddings as produced by, e.g., UMAP or t-SNE. These embeddings can, however, distort the true cluster structure and are known to produc
papers.summary: CAdir is a new method for single-cell RNA-seq clustering that jointly clusters cells and genes, automatically determines the number of clusters, and provides a visualization-driven tool to assess clustering quality. This addresses common limitations of existing algorithms that lack marker gene identification, unsupervised cluster number inference, or reliable quality assessment beyond potentially misleading UMAP/t-SNE plots.

papers.title: Single-cell and high-resolution spatial profiling of podocytopathies reveals core mechanisms of podocyte injury.
papers.abstract: Podocytes (PODs) play a critical role in maintaining glomerular filtration function, and their injury is a key driver of progressive podocytopathies (PCPs). Despite their clinical importance, the molecular and spatial mechanisms underlying POD injury remain poorly understood. We generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and high-resolution spatial transcriptomic (ST) dataset from kidney tissues of patients with five major PCP subtypes. Our analysis revealed distinct molecular signatures among PCP subtypes, injury-related cytoskeletal alterations, and POD-centered microenvironmental
papers.summary: This study generated single-nucleus RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomic data from kidney tissues of patients with five major podocytopathy subtypes, revealing distinct molecular signatures and injury-related cytoskeletal alterations in podocytes. The findings provide a detailed molecular and spatial map of podocyte injury mechanisms, offering potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and machine learning to develop a prognostic signature based on tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The signature identifies key molecular pathways and potential therapeutic targets, offering a new tool for risk stratification and treatment guidance in HNSCC.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial transcriptomics is being applied to study cancer epigenetics, highlighting that traditional sequencing methods lose tissue context crucial for understanding tumor biology. The authors emphasize that spatial technologies can reveal how local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs influence cancer development and progression.

papers.title: SpatialFlux: An R package for distance gradient analysis in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) data analysis and visualization face several challenges due to low sampling, diversity of tissue morphology and high drop-out inherent to the technique. New analysis methods are needed to overcome these challenges and promote continued biological discoveries. To overcome these constraints, we herein describe SpatialFlux, an R package developed to perform reference-based distance gradient analysis. SpatialFlux allows the identification and comprehensive visualization, in either an unbiased or biased manner, of differentially expressed genes and pathways across multi
papers.summary: SpatialFlux is a new R package that analyzes spatial transcriptomics data by measuring gene expression changes along distance gradients from a reference point. It helps identify differentially expressed genes and pathways across tissue regions, addressing challenges like low sampling and high dropout rates.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal SUV39H1 as a master epigenetic driver of immunosuppressive niche and stemness in bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer (BC) exhibits profound molecular heterogeneity and a highly dynamic tumor microenvironment, posing major challenges for effective therapy. In this study, we leveraged single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics, complemented by integrative multi-omics analysis and machine learning, to systematically dissect the cellular and spatial architecture of BC and uncover key regulatory drivers.We identified the histone methyltransferase SUV39H1 as a central epigenetic regulator strongly associated with tumor progression, stemness, and poor prognosis. At single-cell
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify the histone methyltransferase SUV39H1 as a key epigenetic driver that promotes an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and cancer stemness in bladder cancer, linking it to poor prognosis.

papers.title: A Unified Developmental Timeline of Pigmented Ocular Tissues in the Mouse Eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study uses a gentle bleaching method compatible with immunohistochemistry to create a unified developmental timeline of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye, overcoming the historical challenge of melanin interference. By combining this approach with re-analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data, the authors provide a comprehensive atlas of coordinated development across pigmented ocular structures.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis Identifies Stellate Cell-Derived Complement Component 7 as a Predictor of Fibrosis and Liver-Related Events in MASLD Patients.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a growing global health burden, with advanced fibrosis and liver-related events (LREs) being key prognostic factors. However, existing non-invasive biomarkers insufficiently capture both fibrosis severity and LRE risk. This study aimed to identify a mechanistically grounded biomarker for clinical risk stratification.
papers.summary: This study identifies complement component 7 (C7), derived from hepatic stellate cells, as a novel biomarker that predicts both fibrosis severity and liver-related events in patients with MASLD. Using integrative multi-omics analysis, the authors show that C7 outperforms existing non-invasive markers for risk stratification. The finding offers a mechanistically grounded tool for clinical management of MASLD.

papers.title: Leveraging the genetics of human face shape boosts the discovery of orofacial cleft risk loci.
papers.abstract: Several lines of evidence suggest that normal-range facial features and nonsyndromic orofacial clefts (OFCs) exhibit a shared genetic basis. Approaches designed to leverage this relationship hold the possibility of revealing new OFC risk loci by boosting discovery power. To test this idea, we applied a pleiotropy-informed GWAS method (cFDR-GWAS) with summary statistics from large, independent European GWASs of normal facial shape (n=4,680; n=3,566) and nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (nsCL/P, n=3,969). The cFDR approach identified 21 independent genomic loci significantly a
papers.summary: This study shows that using a statistical method that accounts for shared genetic influences between normal facial shape and orofacial clefts can identify new risk loci for clefts that standard GWAS would miss. By combining data from large European studies, the authors found 21 genomic regions linked to cleft risk, demonstrating the power of leveraging related traits to boost discovery.

papers.title: Decoding neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts unveils a shared target reservoir for immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, predominantly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), has limited therapeutic options. While mutation-derived neoantigen vaccine holds promise, its success is hindered by low antigen availability. This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts, neoTSTs) in HCC, characterizing their features, generation mechanisms, and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: This study identifies a new class of neoantigens derived from tumor-specific transcripts (neoTSTs) in hepatocellular carcinoma, which may serve as a shared reservoir for immunotherapy. The findings suggest that these transcriptome-derived neoantigens could overcome the limitation of low antigen availability seen with mutation-based vaccines.

papers.title: Deciphering spatial heterogeneity by multimodal spatial transcriptomics modelling with SpatialModal.
papers.abstract: Advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies have made it possible to jointly acquire gene expression and histological image information while preserving spatial coordinates. This breakthrough presents unprecedented opportunities for the precise dissection of spatial heterogeneity in complex tissues. However, existing computational methods remain limited in their capacity for effective integration and synergistic modelling of multimodal ST data.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SpatialModal, a computational method that integrates gene expression and histological image data from spatial transcriptomics to better understand tissue heterogeneity. It addresses the limitation of existing tools in effectively combining these multimodal data types.

papers.title: Decoding neuronal gene expression: integrative insights from omics and AI.
papers.abstract: Neuronal functional diversity and pathological vulnerability are governed by multi-layered regulatory programs. While high-throughput omics and neuroimaging provide high-resolution snapshots of these programs, bridging the gap between molecular dynamics and macro-scale brain architecture remains a significant informatics challenge. This review synthesizes the evolution of computational frameworks in neuro-omics-transitioning from descriptive co-expression modules to causal graph neural networks and cross-scale foundation models. We evaluate these methodologies within the context of Alzheimer's
papers.summary: This review examines how computational frameworks in neuro-omics have evolved from basic co-expression analysis to advanced graph neural networks and cross-scale models, aiming to connect molecular brain dynamics with large-scale brain architecture. The authors evaluate these methods in the context of Alzheimer's disease, highlighting the challenge of integrating multi-layered omics data with neuroimaging to understand neuronal diversity and disease vulnerability.

papers.title: SRLST: a unified multimodal representation learning framework for spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables molecular profiling within native tissue architecture, yet accurate delineation of spatial domains in ST data is challenging, as it demands the coordinated integration of transcriptomic, spatial, and tissue histological information.
papers.summary: This paper presents SRLST, a unified multimodal representation learning framework that integrates transcriptomic, spatial, and histological data to improve the identification of spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics. The framework outperforms existing methods by effectively combining these diverse data types for more accurate tissue architecture analysis.

papers.title: NodoMap: A single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the mouse nodose ganglion.
papers.abstract: The vagus nerve is a central component of the parasympathetic nervous system, innervating multiple abdominal organs to monitor and regulate their function. Vagal sensory neuron cell bodies reside in the nodose ganglia, but their molecular diversity and spatial organization remain incompletely defined. Here, we generated and integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data with multiple published datasets to construct a unified atlas of 106,436 cells and combined this with spatial transcriptomics to create a single-cell and spatial map of the mouse nodose ganglion (NodoMap). We identif
papers.summary: This study presents NodoMap, a comprehensive single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the mouse nodose ganglion, integrating snRNA-seq data from over 100,000 cells with spatial transcriptomics. The resource maps the molecular diversity and spatial organization of vagal sensory neurons, providing a foundational reference for understanding vagus nerve function.

papers.title: Autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus: insights from integrative multi-omics analyses.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by the emergence of autoantibodies and deposition of immune complexes. SLE presents with heterogeneous multi-organ involvement that varies among patients and its mechanisms have been investigated to facilitate appropriate stratification and treatment selection. Bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq have provided important insights into the pathogenesis of SLE; however, these approaches are inherently limited by their reliance on predefined cell subsets and known markers, which can introduce bias and restrict their ability to fu
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrative multi-omics analyses, including single-cell approaches, are providing new insights into the role of autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), an autoimmune disease with heterogeneous organ involvement. The authors highlight that while bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq have advanced understanding of SLE pathogenesis, these methods are limited by reliance on predefined cell markers, and newer single-cell technologies can overcome these biases to better characterize disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Crosstalk between TFF2+ HCC cells and regulatory T cells drives hepatocellular carcinoma prometastatic niche formation and portal vein tumor thrombosis.
papers.abstract: Portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) is a critical event that promotes intrahepatic dissemination, induces portal hypertension, and worsens the prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet its formation mechanism remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study identifies a crosstalk between TFF2+ HCC cells and regulatory T cells that promotes the formation of a prometastatic niche and portal vein tumor thrombosis in hepatocellular carcinoma. The findings reveal a new mechanism driving PVTT, a key factor in poor HCC prognosis.

papers.title: SPP1-positive macrophages drive trastuzumab resistance in HER2-positive breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Trastuzumab-based HER2-targeted therapy remains the cornerstone treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer. However, its clinical efficacy is significantly modulated by the tumor microenvironment (TME). Our single-cell sequencing analysis of clinical samples revealed that patients with poor radiologic response after trastuzumab-based neoadjuvant therapy presented significant enrichment of TIGIT+ NK cells with high immune checkpoint expression, exhausted CD8+ T cells, and immunosuppressive regulatory T cells (Tregs). Further analyses leveraging cell-cell communication, spatial transcriptomics, a
papers.summary: This study identifies SPP1-positive macrophages as a key driver of trastuzumab resistance in HER2-positive breast cancer. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, the authors show that these macrophages create an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that limits the efficacy of HER2-targeted therapy.

papers.title: The IGF2-ERK-Fos axis drives a Müller cell glial-mesenchymal transition-like response to disrupt retinal homeostasis in early myopia.
papers.abstract: Myopia is increasingly recognized as a complex pathology involving retinal remodeling, yet the cellular mechanisms linking early visual stress to this process remain unclear. This study investigated whether Müller glial (MG) cells undergo a glial-mesenchymal transition (GMT)-like response in early myopia and identified the upstream signaling axis driving this transformation. We integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses to construct a high-resolution atlas of retinal cell heterogeneity in a guinea pig model of form-deprivation myopia (FDM). Single-cell analysis revealed an expa
papers.summary: This study found that in early myopia, Müller glial cells undergo a glial-mesenchymal transition-like response driven by the IGF2-ERK-Fos signaling axis, which disrupts retinal homeostasis. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in a guinea pig model, the researchers identified this cellular transformation as a key mechanism linking visual stress to retinal remodeling in myopia.

papers.title: SpaDiff denoises sequence-based spatial transcriptomics via diffusion process.
papers.abstract: Spot-swapping in sequence-based spatial transcriptomics redistributes RNA molecules across neighboring spots, distorting spatial gene expression and biasing downstream analysis. We introduce SpaDiff, a mass-conserving denoising framework that corrects this artifact through score-guided reverse diffusion. Across simulated and real spatial transcriptomics datasets, SpaDiff consistently improves the recovery of spatial gene-expression distributions. In particle-level simulations with known ground truth, SpaDiff robustly restores gene-level spatial patterns across diverse contamination regimes. In
papers.summary: SpaDiff is a new computational method that corrects spot-swapping artifacts in sequence-based spatial transcriptomics data, where RNA molecules get redistributed across neighboring spots. Using a mass-conserving diffusion process, it improves the recovery of true spatial gene expression patterns, as demonstrated on both simulated and real datasets.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify epigenetic regulators of pluripotency in mouse embryonic stem cells, revealing that Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 antagonistically control the transition between naive and primed pluripotency states. The findings provide new insights into how histone modifications orchestrate cell fate decisions.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal mechanistic insights of FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent and aggressive subtype of renal malignancy, characterized by extensive vascularization and poor prognosis. Early detection markedly improves patient outcomes, and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA, encoded by FOLH1) imaging has recently emerged as a valuable diagnostic tool for ccRCC. However, the cellular source, spatial distribution, and mechanistic contribution of FOLH1 expression within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial multi-omics to identify FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and reveals their potential role in tumor vascularization and progression. The findings provide mechanistic insights into how these cells contribute to the tumor microenvironment, which could inform diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Scalable hypothalamic neuron differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells suitable for modeling metabolic disorders.
papers.abstract: The hypothalamus, composed of multiple nuclei, is essential for maintaining the body's homeostasis. Within the mediobasal hypothalamus, the arcuate nucleus (ARC) contains key neuronal populations, including appetite-suppressing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons that regulate energy and glucose balance. Here, we present a chemically defined, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) into hypothalamic neurons enriched for POMC cells, compatible with robotic cell culture platforms for high-throughput use. Neuronal identity was validated by MERFISH single-cell tran
papers.summary: This paper presents a new, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells into hypothalamic neurons, specifically those that produce the appetite-suppressing protein POMC. The method is chemically defined and compatible with robotic platforms, making it suitable for high-throughput studies of metabolic disorders like obesity and diabetes.

papers.title: Identification of potential diagnostic biomarkers for myocardial infarction using bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction(AMI)is an important type of cardiovascular disease, which seriously threatens the lives of humans. In order to help patients receive timely clinical treatment and improve their survival rates, it is necessary to screen out related molecules in advance. To this end, we applied bioinformatics methods and machine learning algorithms to find possible biomarkers associated with AMI. When considering possible connections with dynamics of immune cells activation. Based on the RNA-seq results, differential expression analysis was performed followed by WGCNA to identify stab
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics and machine learning to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), with a focus on their connection to immune cell activation. The findings could help enable earlier clinical diagnosis and improve patient survival rates.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics identifies CYP1B1 as a candidate molecular link between toxicant exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by progressive airflow limitation, chronic airway inflammation, and epithelial remodeling. Although oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation are increasingly recognized as important contributors to COPD pathobiology, the epithelial biomarkers and regulatory pathways linking cigarette-smoke exposure to ferroptosis-related injury remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to identify CYP1B1 as a potential molecular link between cigarette smoke exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD. The findings suggest that CYP1B1 may serve as a biomarker and therapeutic target for COPD by connecting toxicant exposure to ferroptosis-driven airway injury.

papers.title: PathwayBench: a multi-criterion benchmark of pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods reveals rank-window competition as a mechanism of biological signal loss in single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: Pathway activity scoring is a foundational step in single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analysis, yet method choice is rarely guided by systematic, multi-criterion evidence in the pseudobulk case-control regime that now dominates applied single-cell disease studies. Prior single-cell pathway-scoring benchmarks have focused on perturbation ground truth at cell-level resolution, leaving the donor-level pseudobulk setting - and the question of why methods disagree - largely unaddressed.
papers.summary: This study introduces PathwayBench, a multi-criterion benchmark for evaluating pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods in single-cell RNA-seq case-control studies. The authors find that method disagreement stems from 'rank-window competition,' a mechanism where biological signal is lost when pathway genes compete for rank within a fixed window, and they provide guidance for method selection.

papers.title: Computational spatial transcriptomic re-analysis reveals biofilm-depth-dependent compartmentalization of SOS-associated and DNA-repair transcriptional programs in Escherichia coli.
papers.abstract: Biofilms are spatially structured microbial communities in which local physiological conditions vary across depth, potentially shaping DNA stress responses, repair pathways, and genome-plasticity-associated cellular states. However, the spatial organization of these transcriptional programs within individual bacterial biofilms remains poorly understood. Here, we re-analyzed public RAINBOW-seq spatial transcriptomic data from Escherichia coli BW25113 biofilms (GSE197541) using a curated 73-gene panel encompassing SOS response, stress response, biofilm matrix, conjugation- and competence-associa
papers.summary: This study re-analyzed public spatial transcriptomic data from E. coli biofilms and found that SOS-associated and DNA-repair transcriptional programs are compartmentalized by biofilm depth, with distinct patterns in surface, middle, and bottom layers. The findings reveal that spatial heterogeneity within biofilms influences DNA stress responses and genome plasticity, providing new insights into how bacterial communities organize their stress and repair activities.

papers.title: PLNFGL: joint estimation of multi-condition gene networks from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Graphical models have been widely used in bioinformatics to infer the conditional dependence structure among random variables, but traditional Gaussian graphical models (GGMs) are suboptimal for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) due to dropout events and distributional mismatch. Moreover, most existing methods estimate networks under a single condition, limiting their utility in multi-condition studies.
papers.summary: This paper introduces PLNFGL, a method that jointly estimates gene regulatory networks across multiple conditions from single-cell RNA-seq data, overcoming limitations of traditional Gaussian graphical models that fail to handle dropout events and distributional mismatches in scRNA-seq. By modeling multiple conditions simultaneously, PLNFGL improves network inference accuracy and enables comparative analysis of condition-specific regulatory changes.

papers.title: Identifying condition-related cell-cell communication events using supervised tensor analysis.
papers.abstract: Many tools have been developed to infer active cell-cell communication (CCC) events, which are essential for understanding biological processes and diseases. However, existing methods for assessing the relationships between CCC events and biological conditions have at least one practical limitation: a lack of clear interpretation, an inability to adjust for confounders, or an inability to model inherent dependencies among CCC events. To comprehensively address these limitations, we introduce STACCato, a supervised tensor analysis tool for identifying condition-related CCC events. STACCato empl
papers.summary: STACCato is a new supervised tensor analysis tool that identifies cell-cell communication events related to specific biological conditions, overcoming limitations of existing methods in interpretability, confounder adjustment, and dependency modeling. It enables more accurate discovery of condition-specific intercellular signaling.

papers.title: A pan-cancer single-cell atlas uncovers the role of sex hormones and chromosomes in sex-divergent reprogramming of the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Sex bias is pervasive in tumors; however, how sex chromosomes and hormone-responsive signaling shape the tumor microenvironment (TME) remains insufficiently characterized. Considering the critical impact of the TME on tumor progression and response to immunotherapy, a pan-cancer investigation of sex-specific and cancer-context-dependent TME features is warranted.
papers.summary: This study uses a pan-cancer single-cell atlas to investigate how sex hormones and chromosomes contribute to differences in the tumor microenvironment between males and females. The findings reveal sex-divergent reprogramming of the TME, which may influence tumor progression and immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: PRECISE: A Prognostic Thyrocyte-Derived Gene Signature for Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) exhibits heterogeneous behavior, underscoring the need for effective biomarkers and improved risk stratification methods. We developed a thyrocyte-derived gene signature, Prognostic RNA Expression Cell-specific Integrated Signature (PRECISE), using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and evaluated its prognostic utility across cohorts.
papers.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
papers.summary: Researchers developed a new gene signature called PRECISE, derived from single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of thyrocytes, to better predict outcomes in papillary thyroid carcinoma. The signature aims to improve risk stratification for this cancer, which has variable behavior. Its prognostic value was validated across multiple patient cohorts.

papers.title: An interpretable multi-task whole-slide histopathology AI model for non-small cell lung cancer: Cross-cohort generalisation, spatial attention-transcriptomic integration, and molecular-immune profiling.
papers.abstract: Tumour-node-metastasis staging does not fully explain prognostic heterogeneity in non-small cell lung cancer. We evaluated whether haematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images could estimate histological subtype, pathological stage probabilities, survival risk and spatially grounded biological associations.
papers.summary: This study presents an interpretable AI model that analyzes whole-slide histopathology images from non-small cell lung cancer patients to predict histological subtype, pathological stage, and survival risk, while also integrating spatial attention with transcriptomic data to reveal molecular and immune profiles. The model demonstrates cross-cohort generalizability, offering a potential tool for more precise prognostic stratification beyond traditional staging.

papers.title: Pan-cancer atlas of cellular architecture reveals a nearest-neighbour distance-associated biomechanical-immune axis involving CD4+ memory T cells.
papers.abstract: The systematic link between cellular spatial organization and its biomechanical consequences remains a critical knowledge gap in human oncology.
papers.summary: This study maps the spatial organization of cells across multiple cancer types, revealing a biomechanical-immune axis where the distance between CD4+ memory T cells and other cells correlates with immune activity and tumor stiffness. The findings suggest that cellular proximity influences both mechanical forces and immune responses in tumors.

papers.title: Discovery of hub genes linking oxidative stress to type 2 diabetic sarcopenia using single-cell sequencing and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and sarcopenia demonstrate a significant comorbidity, particularly in the elderly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking them, especially through oxidative stress, remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes involved in T2DM-associated sarcopenia (T2DS) by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning. We analyzed scRNA-seq datasets (GSE244515, GSE268953) to characterize cellular heterogeneity and bulk RNA-seq datasets (GSE202295, GSE226151) for differential expre
papers.summary: This study identifies key genes linking oxidative stress to type 2 diabetes-associated sarcopenia by combining single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with machine learning. The findings reveal potential molecular targets that could help explain the comorbidity between diabetes and muscle wasting in the elderly.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal GUK1 as a Prognostic Biomarker Regulated by the TP53-HSF1 Axis in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Guanylate kinase 1 (GUK1) is crucial for nucleotide metabolism, yet its impact on breast cancer (BC) progression remains poorly defined. The objective of the present study is to investigate GUK1 as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target. Methods: We employed a multi-omics approach integrating The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data, machine learning algorithm, High-Definition spatial transcriptomics (Visium HD), single-cell profiling, molecular docking and experimental validation including in vitro knockdown models and Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR). Results: LASSO regression i
papers.summary: This study identifies GUK1 as a potential prognostic biomarker in breast cancer, showing that its expression is regulated by the TP53-HSF1 axis and is associated with poor outcomes. Using multi-omics data, spatial transcriptomics, and experimental validation, the authors demonstrate that GUK1 knockdown reduces cancer cell proliferation, suggesting it may be a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Decoding early lung adenocarcinoma progression by single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveals a CMA-related prognostic signature.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression from adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS) to minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA) and invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) is accompanied by molecular heterogeneity and tumor microenvironment remodeling. Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) regulates tumor cell homeostasis, metabolic adaptation, and stress responses, but its dynamic alterations and prognostic significance during the AIS/MIA-to-IAC progression of LUAD remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map molecular changes during lung adenocarcinoma progression from early to invasive stages, revealing a chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA)-related gene signature. The authors identify dynamic CMA alterations linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and develop a prognostic signature that may help predict patient outcomes.

papers.title: Plasticizers and prostate cancer: unraveling the link through network toxicology and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Plasticizers, as widespread environmental endocrine disruptors, are increasingly linked to an elevated risk of prostate cancer (PCa). However, the specific molecular mechanisms by which they drive PCa initiation and progression remain incompletely elucidated. Addressing this knowledge gap is crucial for assessing environmental health risks and identifying potential intervention targets.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and machine learning to investigate how plasticizers, which are common environmental chemicals, may contribute to prostate cancer. The authors identify key molecular pathways and potential targets linking plasticizer exposure to cancer development. This work helps clarify the environmental health risks and suggests possible intervention points.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses reveal an aging-associated fibroblast subtype linked to tumor progression in human skin.
papers.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for the development of many cancers, yet the tissue-level mechanisms linking physiological aging to tumor progression remain unclear. Although age-related accumulation of genetic mutations contributes to tumorigenesis, increasing evidence indicates that the aging tissue microenvironment also plays a critical role in shaping cancer susceptibility. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic datasets from healthy human skin and major skin cancers, including melanoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and basal cell carcinoma, to define c
papers.summary: This study identifies a specific aging-associated fibroblast subtype in human skin that may promote tumor progression, using integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. The findings suggest that the aging tissue microenvironment, not just genetic mutations, plays a key role in cancer susceptibility.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal estrogen-mediated vaginal wall microenvironment remodeling and a perivascular reparative niche in postmenopausal pelvic organ prolapse.
papers.abstract: Local estrogen is widely used to improve vaginal mucosal status and relieve menopausal urogenital symptoms in patients with pelvic organ prolapse (POP), yet clinical outcomes are inconsistent. This creates an urgent need to clarify the tissue-specific mechanisms of estrogen action.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial multi-omics to map how estrogen remodels the vaginal wall microenvironment in postmenopausal pelvic organ prolapse, identifying a perivascular reparative niche. The findings help explain inconsistent clinical outcomes of local estrogen therapy by revealing tissue-specific mechanisms of estrogen action.

papers.title: A review on in-silico analysis of immune cell trafficking and interactions with the tumour microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment (TME) contains a diverse mix of cells and components, including cancer cells, immune cells, connective tissue, and biochemical factors; all of these are constantly interacting as well as influencing both the progression and spread of cancer and the ability of the immune system to recognise and respond to it. Accumulating evidence indicates that immune cell trafficking in TMEs is a major factor in determining whether tumours are destroyed by immune defences or evade immune surveillance. However, advances in experimental techniques do not provide a complete picture of
papers.summary: This review discusses how computational methods can be used to study the movement of immune cells within the tumor microenvironment and their interactions with cancer cells. The authors highlight that while experimental techniques are advancing, they do not provide a complete picture, making in-silico analysis a valuable complementary approach for understanding immune cell trafficking and its role in tumor progression or immune evasion.

papers.title: Cell-state transitions and microenvironmental remodeling in thyroid cancer progression revealed by single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Thyroid cancer ranges from indolent differentiated tumors to metastatic, radioiodine-refractory and anaplastic disease. Conventional histology and molecular classification define major risk groups but do not resolve the cell states and spatial heterogeneity that accompany progression. This review integrates recent single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and validation studies across localized papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), metastatic or radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (PDTC) and anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (AT
papers.summary: This review synthesizes findings from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics studies to map how thyroid cancer progresses from indolent to aggressive forms. It reveals that malignant cells undergo distinct state transitions and that the tumor microenvironment is remodeled in a spatially organized manner during progression. These insights help explain why some thyroid cancers become treatment-resistant and metastatic.

papers.title: Perspective on the integration of radiomics and spatial omics in the analysis of the tumor microenvironment of bladder cancer and prospects for precision diagnosis and treatment.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer, a common malignant tumor of the urinary system, possesses a highly heterogeneous tumor immune microenvironment that critically influences disease progression, treatment response, and patient prognosis. The limitations of traditional tissue biopsies have spurred interest in non-invasive, dynamic, and spatially resolved assessment strategies. Radiomics enables non-invasive quantification of macroscopic tumor phenotypes through high-throughput extraction of medical imaging features, while spatial omics technologies, such as single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, reveal the fine-
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how combining radiomics (non-invasive imaging analysis) with spatial omics (like single-cell and spatial transcriptomics) could improve understanding of the tumor microenvironment in bladder cancer. The authors argue that integrating these approaches may enable more precise, non-invasive assessment of tumor heterogeneity and guide personalized treatment decisions.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics and mendelian randomization reveal the critical role of pyroptosis in prognosis and therapy of lung squamous cell carcinomas.
papers.abstract: Most types of programmed cell death (PCD) have been demonstrated to play critical roles in the pathogenesis and prognosis of lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC). However, the specific type of PCD with the most prominent driving effect and regulatory value in LUSC remains unclear.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics data and Mendelian randomization to identify pyroptosis as the most influential programmed cell death type in lung squamous cell carcinoma, affecting prognosis and therapy response. The findings suggest pyroptosis-related genes could serve as prognostic markers and therapeutic targets for LUSC.

papers.title: Multiomics Analysis Reveals CTHRC1+ CAFs Drive Immunosuppressive Niches and Predict Immunotherapy Resistance in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) orchestrate immune-excluded tumor microenvironment (TME), but the CAF heterogeneity remains incompletely understood in gastric cancer (GC). In this study, we integrated multicohort single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data to construct a comprehensive atlas of the GC TME. Unsupervised clustering identified eight transcriptionally distinct CAF subpopulations, among which CTHRC1+ CAFs were selectively enriched in tumors and showed the strongest association with T cell exclusion. Pseudotemporal trajectory ana
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data to create a comprehensive atlas of the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment, identifying eight distinct cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subpopulations. The CTHRC1+ CAF subtype is selectively enriched in tumors and strongly associated with T cell exclusion, suggesting it drives immunosuppressive niches and may predict immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Multi-omics comparison of periodontitis and peri-implantitis identifies plasma cell enrichment as a shared feature and a periodontitis-associated endothelial-plasma cell APP-CD74 axis.
papers.abstract: To define the shared and divergent immune architecture of periodontitis (PD) and peri-implantitis (PI) and to identify intercellular communication programs linked to plasma cell accumulation.
papers.summary: This study compared the immune profiles of periodontitis and peri-implantitis using multi-omics, finding that both diseases share an enrichment of plasma cells. A key discovery was a periodontitis-specific interaction between endothelial and plasma cells involving the APP-CD74 signaling axis, which may drive plasma cell accumulation.

papers.title: Integrated bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic analyses prioritize NOTCH1 as a candidate gene associated with neurovascular and immune-related alterations in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is classically defined by dopaminergic neurodegeneration in the substantia nigra, yet how immune activation is linked to neurovascular dysfunction in the diseased brain remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics to identify NOTCH1 as a key gene linking neurovascular and immune changes in Parkinson's disease. The findings suggest that NOTCH1 may play a role in the interaction between blood vessels and immune cells in the brain, offering a new target for understanding PD pathology.
